policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'a great voice' fixes the English adjective before its noun whichever order the Greek has, so μεγάλης φωνῆς and φωνῆς μεγάλης are indistinguishable here.
Present ἐκχέετε and aorist ἐκχέατε are both imperatives rendered 'pour out'; ASV marks no aspectual difference in an imperative.
ASV 'And the second poured out his bowl' names no angel, so the added ἄγγελος is not the text it rendered.
ASV's note on 'every living soul' reads 'Greek soul of life', mapping ψυχὴ ζωῆς rather than the attributive ψυχὴ ζῶσα.
ASV 'even the things that were in the sea' renders the substantival τὰ; without it the phrase would be a bare prepositional adjunct with nothing to carry 'the things'.
ASV 'into the rivers and the fountains of the waters' shares one preposition across both nouns, which is its ordinary practice whether or not the Greek repeats εἰς.
ASV 'thou Holy One' renders ὅσιος as a substantive, which the surrounding string of articular participles supports with or without this article.
ASV 'blood hast thou given them to drink' is a perfect, and the same verse renders the aorist ἔκρινας as 'thou didst thus judge', so its tenses distinguish δέδωκας from ἔδωκας.
ASV 'And the fourth poured out his bowl' names no angel, so the added ἄγγελος is not the text it rendered.
ASV 'to scorch men with fire' puts object before instrument as English requires, so it does not report the Greek order.
ASV 'and they blasphemed' continues with a pronoun; the added οἱ ἄνθρωποι would repeat the subject ASV had just written as 'men were scorched'.
The variant is the article alone, and ASV 'hath the power over these plagues' supplies English definiteness idiomatically rather than as a report of τὴν.
The variant is one article in a chain of three, and ASV 'the great river, the river Euphrates' is definite throughout regardless of which one stands.
ASV 'three unclean spirits' fixes the English order of numeral and adjective, so τρία ἀκάθαρτα and ἀκάθαρτα τρία are indistinguishable.
ASV 'the war of the great day of God' renders no demonstrative, so the added ἐκείνης ('that day') is not the text it followed.
ASV distinguishes the two prepositions within the verse — 'out of the temple, from the throne' — rendering ἐκ and ἀπό differently, so ἐκ is the reading behind 'out of'.
ASV 'out of the temple' has no 'of heaven', so the added τοῦ οὐρανοῦ is not the text it rendered.
ASV lists 'lightnings, and voices, and thunders' in the base order; it follows the Greek order of such lists rather than reordering them.
ASV 'and there was a great earthquake' sets none of its words in italics, so 'there was' renders ἐγένετο rather than supplying a verb the Greek lacks.

ASV 'since there were men upon the earth' is plural and its note 'Some ancient authorities read there was a man' maps the singular ἄνθρωπος ἐγένετο as the reading it did not follow; the remaining article does not surface in English.
